coordinates.locator: area centroid of OpenStreetMap way 87723028 ('Reaktorgebäude', Kernkraftwerk Brokdorf; element version 6, last edited 2025-11-27, read from the OSM API on 2026-10-28; the same outline is in the 2026-10-25 extract)
coordinates.note: Campus-grade point at the reactor-building complex (the outline spans about 130 m), shown as approximate. The CONUS detector sat 17.1 m from the reactor core inside this building (arXiv:2401.07684), but no source gives a more precise position.

name: Brokdorf Nuclear Power Plant campus
notes: The CONUS detector itself sat 17.1 m from the reactor core inside the plant (arXiv:2011.00210); no separate, more precise detector-hall coordinate was found in a fetched source, so this campus-level point is used for the site record.

summary.plain: A now-closed nuclear power plant on the Elbe river in northern Germany, where the CONUS experiment sat just 17 metres from the reactor core to catch its antineutrinos.
summary.technical: Surface site of the (now shut down) Brokdorf pressurised water reactor, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany; hosted the CONUS CEvNS detector 17.1 m from the reactor core, 2018-2022 data taking before the 2023 move to Leibstadt.
